raw_response:
I will still do what has worked on my land, then adjust a little from last year. I farm 20 mu, so I cannot gamble with yield. On wheat, I will keep improved seed, put the main fertilizer down early, and use my well for the key waterings. Around here, if wheat is short of fertilizer or misses water at jointing and filling, the loss shows fast, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the heads stay light. On maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people here do, because I have seen it yield better on neighboring fields. I will keep fertilizer a bit heavy on nitrogen, but not blindly, because too much also wastes money and can push weak growth. Since some family members work off-farm, I will choose tillage and field work that saves labor and lets me finish on time. I will do roughly what good growers nearby do: stable fertilizer, enough water from the well, and pesticide sprays when I see real pressure, not just for show.
